results.questionText: If the documentation gap in the design doc that Jax contributed to on Day 4 had not existed, would the incident still have occurred despite the other gaps involving Raj and Kaitlyn?
results.groundedQuestion: If the documentation gap in the design doc that Jax contributed to on Day 4 (approx. 2026-01-06) had not existed, would the incident still have occurred despite the other gaps involving Raj and Kaitlyn?
results.agentAnswer:
Hey Jax — honest answer: I can't determine counterfactually whether the incident would have occurred without that design-doc gap, because the company records don't tie that specific documentation gap to the incident's causal chain.

Here's what I found when I searched across Confluence, Slack, PRs, and retrospectives:

- The incident you're referring to (the Kafka telemetry outage, discussed ~2026-01-25 in #engineering_backend) had a documented root-cause discussion: auth-service container logs, Kafka consumer lag, Redis cache behavior, Terraform VPC tag drift, and missing integration test coverage under network degradation were all named as contributing factors [source:slack_engineering_backend_2026-01-26T15:59:35.527814].
- The design doc you contributed to on Day 4 (approx. 2026-01-06) is CONF-ENG-040 "Design: clarify incident reporting process," authored by Karen [source:CONF-ENG-040]. It codifies triage/hand-off workflow for Kafka-consumer-failure incidents.
- The Day 6 incident in Sprint #1 retro was actually about a missing cost-tag on an EKS node group throttling the pacing microservice, not the Kafka telemetry outage [source:CONF-RETRO-001]. The Kafka-related items in that retro are ORG-106/107/109 (scaling and alert threshold tickets), not a design-doc gap.
- I did not find any postmortem, RCA section, Slack thread, or Jira ticket that names Jax, Raj, or Kaitlyn as owners of documentation gaps that caused the Kafka telemetry incident. The only Kaitlyn reference nearby is a compliance-docs Zoom on 2026-01-28 [source:zoom_2026-01-28_4aaed546], and the only Raj references are about postmortem sync tooling and CloudWatch alarm lookups in later months [source:slack_engineering_mobile_2026-02-20T15:41:00] [source:slack_digital-hq_2026-03-16T10:10:00].

So the framing of your question — three distinct documentation gaps owned by you, Raj, and Kaitlyn as co-causes of one incident — doesn't match what's in the records. What the records do show is a cluster of independent gaps (missing integration test coverage, Terraform tag drift, incomplete scaling ticket, no SLA on alert thresholds) where documentation was symptomatic rather than causal.

If you can point me to the specific incident ticket or postmortem you're thinking of (a Jira key or Confluence page ID would help), I can give you a sharper counterfactual read.
